title: All Nine Award Winners in Japan’s NEDO Quantum Challenge Leverage IBM Hardware; Four Dedicated Industry Sponsor Prizes Awarded - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Japan's NEDO (under METI) announced Season 1 winners of its quantum prize challenge from 87 entries: all nine general-track winners used IBM Quantum hardware (six exclusively), and 65 of 80 teams (81%) chose IBM, logging 11,159 jobs and 5,900+ QPU minutes. Judges led by Prof. Keisuke Fujii withheld first prizes in two of three tracks over strict classical-advantage standards; Shionogi won 1st in Quality of Life with quantum-HPC drug discovery, and Season 2 is focused on commercialization.

themes.theme: IBM dominance in Japan's quantum challenge

insights.claim: All nine general-track award winners in NEDO's Season 1 quantum challenge did their research on IBM Quantum hardware, and six relied exclusively on IBM superconducting systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM holds de facto platform lock-in among Japanese industrial quantum users; a mindshare signal versus rivals.
insights.quote: All nine general track award winners conducted their research on IBM Quantum hardware, with six relying exclusively on IBM superconducting systems

insights.claim: Across the challenge, 65 of 80 participating teams (81%) chose IBM Quantum Platform systems, logging 11,159 execution jobs and over 5,900 minutes of QPU time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hard usage metrics showing IBM's cloud QPU share in a national program.
insights.quote: 65 of the 80 participating teams (81%) selected IBM Quantum Platform systems, logging 11,159 execution jobs

insights.claim: IBM's Jay Gambetta said participants' success was accelerated by pairing hardware with third-party software via Qiskit Functions, citing Q-CTRL's error-mitigation tooling and Kipu Quantum's Iskay algorithm.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's software catalog ecosystem deepens lock-in and benefits partners like Q-CTRL and Kipu Quantum.

insights.claim: The judging committee chaired by Prof. Keisuke Fujii of Kyoto University declined to award first place in the Society 5.0 and Cool Japan tracks and withheld the Jury Chairman's Special Award, setting a high bar for claims of verifiable advantage over classical supercomputing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Expert judges found no project clearing a strict classical-advantage bar; temper near-term quantum utility claims.
insights.quote: setting a high threshold for projects claiming verifiable advantages over classical supercomputing

insights.claim: The program drew 87 submissions: 46 in Society 5.0, 25 in Quality of Life and 16 in Cool Japan, with nine general prizes awarded.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Broad corporate participation shows Japanese industry is actively exploring quantum use cases.

insights.claim: Shionogi won first place in Quality of Life (¥40M, ~$255,000) for quantum-HPC hybrid drug discovery evaluating intermolecular binding energy and structure generation via Deep QSCI.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A listed Japanese pharma is the top winner; quantum-HPC chemistry is the most credible near-term use case.

insights.claim: KDDI Research's Q-Chainners tied for third in Society 5.0 with blockchain transaction security using gate-based quantum hash generation across four IBM QPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Telecom players are probing quantum for security; small-scale experiment.

insights.claim: A Mitsubishi Chemical, Keio, ASU and IBM team tied for third in Cool Japan for multi-objective hybrid optimization of low-carbon chemical synthesis on the University of Tokyo IBM System One.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Large chemical incumbents engage quantum via IBM's domestic System One.

insights.claim: Two winning teams, Q4Health (antimicrobial microbiome engineering using Kipu Quantum's Iskay) and EntangleTune (quantum timbre generation for music), were spun out as startups.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Prize programs are seeding Japanese quantum startups; early-stage pipeline.

insights.claim: The private-sector WIRED Quantum Partnership, sponsored by Quantinuum, Mitsui & Co., Mitsubishi Estate and Toshiba, gave four sponsor awards, including Toshiba's for large-scale quantum annealing for UAV flight routing and swarm control and Quantinuum's for power distribution network optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Japanese conglomerates and Quantinuum are using sponsorship to scout applications and partners.

insights.claim: NEDO will publish a case-study collection in December 2026 and an R&D barrier analysis report in March 2027, while Season 2 research (2026-2027) is already underway with a focus on startup incubation, business models and corporate technology transfer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Japan's government is shifting from prize research to commercialization; watch for partner-matching outcomes.
